successors.name: Achaemenid Empire
successors.text: the Peshawar valley (Gandara satrapy, from c.

ledger.x: c. 600 BCE: Gandhara, ruled from Taksasila and Puskalavati, holds the Peshawar valley, the Indus crossing and Kashmir. 'By the 6th century BCE, Gandhara had expanded to include the valley of Kasmira'; rulers 'c. 700 BCE: Nagnajit', 'c. 550 BCE: Pukkusati'; the Madrakas, Kekayas, Usinaras and Shivis were 'under…

c. 535 BCE: Cyrus the Great annexes Gandhara west of the Indus. 'Around 535 BCE' the Persian army 'annexed a large region to the west of the Indus River'; 'Cyrus probably went as far as the banks of the Indus river' and organised it as the Gandhara satrapy, 'the entire Peshawar Valley' bounded by Swat, Afghanistan…

c. 518 BCE: Darius I's army reaches the Jhelum; Taksasila falls and Gandhara ends as a kingdom. 'Around 518 BCE' the army pushed 'to the Jhelum River', 'secure occupation of Gandhara' is dated to this year, and the Behistun inscription (c. 518 BCE) lists Gandara; the Hindush satrapy, 'the Greater Punjab region'…

wars.name: Achaemenid conquest of the Indus Valley
wars.outcome: 'Persian victory'; 'Annexation of the Indus Valley by the Persians': the Gandhara satrapy under Cyrus (c.

wars.name: Pukkusati's war with Pradyota of Avanti
wars.outcome: 'Pukkusati was successful in this struggle with Pradyota'; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Pukkusati's war with the Pandavas
wars.outcome: 'war broke out between him and the Pandava tribe'; outcome and land not given.

certainty.note: The Indus is the only line the pages give (Cyrus's annexation 'to the west of the Indus River'); the Kashmir and Swat edges are the gazetteer's regions.
